name: Keratosis palmaris et plantaris-clinodactyly syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse or focal hyperkeratosis on the palms and soles
Clinodactyly of one or more fingers, typically the fifth digit
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Exclusion of other syndromes with keratoderma and digital anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of palmar-plantar keratosis and clinodactyly with exclusion of other syndromes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; genetic testing may be supportive but no specific gene identified.

imaging: Radiographs showing clinodactyly with mild curvature of the fifth digit
genetic: No specific gene identified; suspected autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic keratoderma and digital anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Transgrediens pattern of keratoderma extending beyond palms and soles

redFlags: Rapid progression of keratoderma with ulceration
Severe pain or functional impairment of hands or feet
Signs of secondary infection in keratoderma lesions
references: Orphanet: Keratosis palmaris et plantaris-clinodactyly syndrome - ORPHA:86919
Syndromes of the Skin, 4th Edition, Roger A. Haber
